top_comments.text:
Even if a steer is finished on grain, if it lives 2 years, it may only be on grain the last 6 months of its life. It may only be 4 months, and it's never over 8 months. So, let's not go crazy on this. Grain farming at big scale is nasty to the planet, and feed lots do contribute to this. But it's only a small part of a steer's life. Sure, eat grass finished if you can afford it! But let's not totally demonize feedlot finishing. It's not as bad as some say.  Even if it is slaughtered between 18 mo and 2 years, it's still mainly on grass. 

You need to focus much more on how bad the case is that beef ranching/raising is "bad" for the earth and so on. Yes, they mislead on water use. Farming (growing grain and veg and so on) uses vastly, VASTLY more irrigation water from wells, lakes and rivers. Farming is VERY destructive of the land. Most urbanites have never walked on a row crop farm. They fly over them, they drive past them - oh that's corn. How nice. But no, it's not nice. A corn field is a vast area of wasteland - of bare soil, fence and crop - and nothing else. Almost nothing else. Few bugs. Almost no weeds. Nothing for wildlife to eat or live on. And there is almost no wildlife in a typical crop farm. And if animals appear or move in, the farmer kills them. Shoots them, poisons them, traps them. In huge numbers. And plowing kills who-knows how many wildlife animals. Birds, lizards, deer, bunnies, field mice, and on and on. Also, zillions - untold zillions - of animals can't exist - never get a chance to live. Because the land is controlled and offers them no food, most of the year. And if a field goes fallow and critters move in - here comes a tractor the size of a small house towing a 42 foot wide (or wider) steel implement of death and destruction.

Ranching is different. It uses land that's not good for crop growing. It's too steep or hilly. The soil is too poor - grass grows okay but crops would need mega-doses of chem fertilizer. Or mega doses of domesticated animal manure, which comes from people eating meat. The soil may be too rocky. It may be hard pan. Or enough rain for grass, but not enough for crops. So this idea that cow growing "steals land" from more efficient "calorie per acre" farming is total bullsh*t. Most of the earth is not suitable for cropping - for normal ag to grow plants. Or it would require destructive interventions - and expensive ones. Most of the earth is not only suitable for ranching, the biome has always had a ruminant/soil/plant relationship that keeps the biome healthy. In the past it may have been a mix of bison, elk, deer and such - and now it's cows. But it's ruminants. Soil and biomes thrive with ruminants grazing. It's unnatural to remove the ruminants - and you're making a wasteland (of crop and dirt) if you farm it for plants.

The loss of topsoil - this is from plant growing. Not ranching. And this is a gigantic problem. The herbicides. Pesticides. Not much used in ranching and shouldn't be used at all. Rare. In farming common. "Oh but I eat organic." So? Organic farmers use poisons too! People don't realize this! It's only a different list, but arguably some organic list poisons are worse than what non-organic farmers use!

When vegans say they get a guilt-free lunch, this is complete bullsh*t. Ignorance. Plant eaters kill more critters - wildlife - than beef eating carnivores do. Vastly more. Especially when we consider carnivores who eat grass finished. Which is a trend we're promoting. Cattle ranches are like wildlife preserves. Not perfectly so, but basically so, yet. Farms are wasteland. Oh once the crop is picked or harvested, for a few weeks, migrating birds and things move in - pick what falls onto the ground and eat it. And then leave. Again, this is land permanently deprived of use by wildlife. Where on a cattle ranch, zillions of songbirds, lizards, field mice, armadillos, and on and on - they thrive.
